disposition.note:
Diagnosis: Croup (barking cough) caused by COVID-19 infection

What is Croup?
Your baby has croup, a condition where a viral infection causes swelling in the airway, leading to a barking cough, hoarse voice, and sometimes noisy breathing (called stridor). Croup symptoms are often worse at night and may last 3–5 days. Because the croup is caused by COVID-19, your baby is contagious and will need to stay home during recovery.

Treatment Given in Clinic Today
Dexamethasone 5 mg by mouth — a single-dose steroid to reduce airway swelling. This is the only dose needed. It begins working within 2 hours and lasts up to 72 hours.

Home Care Instructions

Comfort and Breathing:
Keep your baby calm and comfortable. Crying and agitation can worsen the cough and noisy breathing.
Use cool mist from a humidifier in the bedroom at night.
If the barking cough worsens suddenly at night, take your baby outside into cool night air for 10–15 minutes — this can help reduce airway swelling.
Keep your baby upright or slightly elevated during sleep if possible.

Fever and Pain:
For fever or discomfort, give infant acetaminophen (Tylenol) as directed for weight (ask your provider for the correct dose for 8.5 kg).
Do NOT give ibuprofen (Motrin) to infants under 6 months. At 10 months old, ibuprofen may be used if recommended by your provider.
Do NOT give aspirin.

Fluids and Feeding:
Offer small, frequent feedings (breast milk, formula, or age-appropriate fluids).
Watch for signs of dehydration: fewer than 4 wet diapers in 24 hours, no tears when crying, dry mouth, or unusual sleepiness.

Cough:
Do NOT give over-the-counter cough or cold medicines to infants. They are not safe for children under 2 years old.

COVID-19 Isolation Precautions
Keep your baby home and away from other children, elderly family members, and anyone with a weakened immune system.
Caregivers should wash hands frequently, especially before and after touching the baby.
Isolation should continue for at least 10 days from when symptoms started AND until fever has been gone for at least 24 hours without fever-reducing medicine AND symptoms are improving.
Clean and disinfect frequently touched surfaces daily.

Eye Discharge Care
Gently clean any eye discharge with a warm, damp washcloth, wiping from the inner corner outward.
Use a separate clean cloth for each eye.
If the discharge becomes thick, yellow/green, or the eye becomes very red or swollen, call your provider.

When to Return to Clinic
Call your provider if:
The barking cough is not improving after 3–5 days
Fever lasts more than 5 days or returns after going away
Your baby is not drinking fluids or has fewer wet diapers
Symptoms worsen despite the steroid treatment given today

Call 911 or Go to the Emergency Room Immediately If:
Your baby has noisy breathing (stridor) while resting or sleeping
You see the skin pulling in around the ribs, neck, or breastbone with each breath (retractions)
Your baby's lips or fingernails turn blue or gray
Your baby is drooling and unable to swallow
Your baby becomes very sleepy, limp, or difficult to wake
Your baby is struggling to breathe or breathing very fast

Follow-Up
No routine follow-up is needed if your baby improves as expected.
Call the clinic if symptoms are not improving within 3–5 days or if you have any concerns.
